A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including material relocated from the main text to appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original counterfactual preference evaluations, human annotations, training-data analyses, and CDA fine-tuning experiments in Sections 3–5.

after.justification: v3 retains those original empirical results and adds confidence intervals and annotation-agreement results in Appendices D–E.

M1.justification: The RATE counterfactual-testing procedure and CDA pipeline remain unchanged: annotate biases, perturb rejected responses, optionally supplement training examples, and fine-tune reward models. The generation and labeling prompts are retained.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Chatbot Arena queries, synthetic opinion queries, KIWI-based scientific queries, Skywork training data, and RewardBench evaluation across five biases. v3 names constituent Skywork datasets without establishing additional dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: The same four Gemma/Llama reward-model checkpoints, base-versus-CDA comparisons, and GPT-4o, Claude 3.7 Sonnet, and Gemini 2.5 Pro evaluators are retained. Newly cited mitigation methods are not added as experimental comparators.

E3.justification: The newly reported annotation-reliability analysis introduces weighted agreement: unanimous votes score 1 and 2–1 votes score 2/3, excluding ties and fully split votes (Appendix E). The retained experiments' query counts, annotation collection, model configurations, and training budgets are unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix E adds an analysis of annotation consistency across the five biases. Existing correlation analyses, the vagueness failure case, and joint-debiasing analysis are retained; relocating Table 2 and Figures 6–7 does not introduce new analyses.

E5.justification: Beyond the existing graphical error bars, v3 adds systematic 95% confidence intervals for skew and miscalibration changes across all five bias-specific CDA comparisons, specifying two-proportion z-intervals (Table 5). Table 6 additionally reports weighted annotation agreement. Neither addition establishes extra training runs or seeds.

E6.justification: Tables 5–6 add interval estimates and annotation-agreement results, with agreement ranging from 71.9% to 85.7%. Figure 3 changes the sycophancy cell where neither response exhibits the bias from 91.4% to 91.5%. The headline results and plotted content of Figures 2 and 4–7 are retained.

T1.justification: Equations 1–5, the counterfactual formulation, and the correlation definitions remain unchanged. The new statistical summaries introduce no theoretical propositions, proofs, or substantive mathematical derivations.

C1.justification: The core contributions remain diagnosing five preference-model biases, connecting them to training-data artifacts, and mitigating them with CDA. Both abstracts report miscalibration decreasing from 39.4% to 32.5% while maintaining RewardBench performance.

C2.justification: The abstract replaces the suggestion that biases originate in human-training-data artifacts with an emphasis that this connection remains poorly understood. This modestly qualifies the framing; the detailed amplification interpretation, overcorrection explanation, and Section 8 limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 identifies Skywork constituent datasets and documents annotation filtering, retained counts, and statistical calculations in Appendices D–E. Appendix F adds an explicit LLM-usage disclosure. Checkpoint identifiers, hyperparameters, prompts, and the code/data access destination are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds Shen et al. on length bias, Zhang et al. on format bias, and Wang et al. on reward-model adjustment using data quality. These modestly extend the existing positioning. Consolidating the Singhal preprint and publication references does not remove a distinct work.

P1.justification: There are limited abstract, introduction, and related-work edits, conference-header changes, and appendix reorganization. RewardBench and joint-debiasing discussion moves into Appendix B.1, and Appendices D–F are added. Most prose and the main section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: The document changes from a predominantly two-column layout to a single-column conference format. Figure 1 is restyled and relocated; Table 2 and Figures 6–7 move to appendices; Figure 3 reorders panels; and Tables 5–6 are added. Tables and prompt boxes are extensively reflowed.

improvement.justification: Tables 5–6 improve transparency about CDA uncertainty and human-label reliability. For example, the length-miscalibration interval includes zero, whereas jargon and vagueness intervals exclude zero. These additions make the evidence easier to assess, but the experiments remain unchanged and the main conclusions receive little qualification from the new uncertainty reporting.
